metadata.title: Visualizing Data using t-SNE
metadata.authors: Laurens van der Maaten, Geoffrey Hinton

nodes.name: Map / Map points
nodes.statement: The low-dimensional data representation $Y = \{y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n\}$ obtained from the high-dimensional data $X = \{x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n\}$ is called a $\textit{map}$, and individual $y_i$ are called $\textit{map points}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A map is the low-dimensional embedding of the high-dimensional data, with individual map points being the embedded representations of each datapoint.

nodes.name: Conditional probability $p_{j|i}$ (high-dimensional similarity)
nodes.statement: For high-dimensional points $x_i, x_j$ and Gaussian variance $\sigma_i$: $p_{j|i} = \frac{\exp(-\|x_i - x_j\|^2 / 2\sigma_i^2)}{\sum_{k \neq i} \exp(-\|x_i - x_k\|^2 / 2\sigma_i^2)}$, with $p_{i|i} = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: The probability that $x_i$ would pick $x_j$ as a neighbor under a Gaussian centered at $x_i$ with variance $\sigma_i^2$.

nodes.name: Conditional probability $q_{j|i}$ (low-dimensional similarity, SNE)
nodes.statement: For map points with variance $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$: $q_{j|i} = \frac{\exp(-\|y_i - y_j\|^2)}{\sum_{k \neq i} \exp(-\|y_i - y_k\|^2)}$, with $q_{i|i} = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Low-dimensional analogue of $p_{j|i}$ using a Gaussian with fixed variance $1/\sqrt{2}$ on map points.

nodes.name: Perplexity
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Perp}(P_i) = 2^{H(P_i)}$, where $H(P_i) = -\sum_j p_{j|i} \log_2 p_{j|i}$ is the Shannon entropy of $P_i$ in bits. Interpreted as a smooth measure of the effective number of neighbors.
nodes.statement_clean: Perplexity is two raised to the Shannon entropy of the conditional distribution; it acts as a smooth count of effective neighbors.

nodes.name: Symmetrized joint probability $p_{ij}$
nodes.statement: To avoid outlier issues, define $p_{ij} = \frac{p_{j|i} + p_{i|j}}{2n}$, ensuring $\sum_j p_{ij} > \frac{1}{2n}$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Symmetrize the conditional probabilities and divide by $2n$ so each datapoint contributes meaningfully to the cost.

nodes.name: Symmetric SNE low-dimensional joint $q_{ij}$
nodes.statement: $q_{ij} = \frac{\exp(-\|y_i - y_j\|^2)}{\sum_{k \neq l} \exp(-\|y_k - y_l\|^2)}$, with $q_{ii} = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Joint Gaussian similarity between map points used by symmetric SNE.

nodes.name: t-SNE low-dimensional joint $q_{ij}$ (Student-t with one d.o.f.)
nodes.statement_clean: Joint similarity in the map under a heavy-tailed Student-t distribution with one degree of freedom.

nodes.name: Crowding problem
nodes.statement: When mapping a high-dimensional manifold to two dimensions, the area available for moderately distant points is too small relative to nearby points, so accurately modeling small distances forces moderately distant points much too far away, crushing clusters at the center.
nodes.statement_clean: The geometric mismatch by which low-dimensional space cannot accommodate the volume of moderately distant neighbors of high-dimensional points.

nodes.name: Diffusion distance
nodes.statement: $D^{(t)}(x_i, x_j) = \sqrt{\sum_k \frac{(p_{ik}^{(t)} - p_{jk}^{(t)})^2}{\psi(x_k)^{(0)}}}$, where $p_{ij}^{(t)}$ is the probability of a particle traveling from $x_i$ to $x_j$ in $t$ timesteps.
nodes.statement_clean: Distance between $x_i, x_j$ measured by squared differences of $t$-step random-walk probabilities, weighted by local density.

nodes.name: SNE optimization problem
nodes.statement: Minimize $C = \sum_i \mathrm{KL}(P_i \| Q_i) = \sum_i \sum_j p_{j|i} \log \frac{p_{j|i}}{q_{j|i}}$ over the map $Y$.
nodes.statement_clean: Find the map $Y$ that minimizes the sum of KL divergences between high- and low-dimensional conditional neighbor distributions.

nodes.name: Symmetric SNE optimization problem
nodes.statement: Minimize $C = \mathrm{KL}(P \| Q) = \sum_i \sum_j p_{ij} \log \frac{p_{ij}}{q_{ij}}$ where $P$ and $Q$ are joint distributions over pairs of points.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize a single KL divergence between joint high- and low-dimensional pair distributions.

nodes.name: t-SNE optimization problem
nodes.statement: Minimize $C = \mathrm{KL}(P \| Q)$ where $p_{ij}$ is the symmetrized Gaussian joint and $q_{ij}$ is the Student-t (one d.o.f.) joint defined in Equation 4.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize KL divergence between symmetric Gaussian high-dimensional joint and heavy-tailed Student-t low-dimensional joint.

nodes.name: Combinatorial Dirichlet problem (random walk probabilities)
nodes.statement: Compute the probability that a random walk from a non-landmark point first hits a given landmark point by minimizing the combinatorial Dirichlet integral $D[x] = \frac{1}{2} x^T L x$ subject to landmark boundary conditions, where $L = D - W$ is the graph Laplacian.
nodes.statement_clean: Find first-hit probabilities of random walks via the combinatorial Dirichlet problem on the graph Laplacian.

nodes.name: SNE gradient
nodes.statement: $\frac{\delta C}{\delta y_i} = 2 \sum_j (p_{j|i} - q_{j|i} + p_{i|j} - q_{i|j})(y_i - y_j)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gradient of the SNE cost with respect to $y_i$, interpretable as spring forces.

nodes.name: Gradient update with momentum
nodes.statement: $Y^{(t)} = Y^{(t-1)} + \eta \frac{\delta C}{\delta Y} + \alpha(t)(Y^{(t-1)} - Y^{(t-2)})$, where $\eta$ is the learning rate and $\alpha(t)$ the momentum.
nodes.statement_clean: Iterative parameter update combining gradient step with momentum from prior iterations.

nodes.name: Symmetric SNE gradient
nodes.statement: $\frac{\delta C}{\delta y_i} = 4 \sum_j (p_{ij} - q_{ij})(y_i - y_j)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Simpler-form gradient of the symmetric SNE cost.

nodes.name: t-SNE gradient
nodes.statement: $\frac{\delta C}{\delta y_i} = 4 \sum_j (p_{ij} - q_{ij})(y_i - y_j)(1 + \|y_i - y_j\|^2)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gradient of the t-SNE KL cost; derivation in Appendix A.

nodes.name: Sammon mapping cost function
nodes.statement: $C = \frac{1}{\sum_{ij} \|x_i - x_j\|} \sum_{i \neq j} \frac{(\|x_i - x_j\| - \|y_i - y_j\|)^2}{\|x_i - x_j\|}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sammon mapping cost: weighted squared error between high- and low-dimensional pairwise distances.

nodes.name: Diffusion maps cost
nodes.statement_clean: Diffusion maps minimize squared error between diffusion distances and Euclidean distances in the map.

nodes.name: t-SNE (simple version)
nodes.statement: Gradient-descent-with-momentum procedure that computes high-dimensional affinities $p_{ij}$ at fixed perplexity, then iteratively updates the map $Y$ using the t-SNE gradient (Equation 5).
input: Optimization parameters: number of iterations $T$, learning rate $\eta$, momentum $\alpha(t)$
nodes.pseudocode:
begin
  compute pairwise affinities $p_{j|i}$ with perplexity Perp (using Equation 1)
  set $p_{ij} = (p_{j|i} + p_{i|j}) / 2n$
  sample initial solution $Y^{(0)} = \{y_1, \ldots, y_n\}$ from $\mathcal{N}(0, 10^{-4} I)$
  for $t = 1$ to $T$ do
    compute low-dimensional affinities $q_{ij}$ (using Equation 4)
    compute gradient $\delta C / \delta Y$ (using Equation 5)
    set $Y^{(t)} = Y^{(t-1)} + \eta \, \delta C / \delta Y + \alpha(t)(Y^{(t-1)} - Y^{(t-2)})$
  end
end

nodes.name: Random-walk t-SNE for large data sets
nodes.section: 5 Applying t-SNE to Large Data Sets
nodes.statement: Modification of t-SNE that defines $p_{j|i}$ between landmark points as the fraction of random walks (with edge probabilities $\propto e^{-\|x_i - x_j\|^2}$) starting at landmark $x_i$ that terminate at landmark $x_j$ on a $k$-nearest-neighbor graph built from the entire data set.
output: Low-dimensional map of the landmark points reflecting structure of the entire data set

nodes.name: Early exaggeration
nodes.statement: Optimization trick that multiplies all $p_{ij}$ by a constant (e.g., 4) during the initial iterations to encourage tight, well-separated clusters that can rearrange globally.
output: Modified $p_{ij}$ used in the early phase of optimization

nodes.name: Early compression
nodes.statement: Add an $L_2$ penalty proportional to the sum of squared distances of map points from the origin to keep them close together early in optimization.
input: Iteration at which penalty is removed
output: Modified cost function used in early iterations

nodes.name: Sammon mapping
nodes.statement: Nonlinear projection that minimizes the Sammon cost function via Newton's method, weighting pairwise-distance errors by the inverse of high-dimensional distance.

nodes.name: Isomap
nodes.statement: Manifold-learning method that approximates geodesic distances on a $k$-nearest-neighbor graph and embeds them via classical multidimensional scaling.

nodes.name: Locally Linear Embedding (LLE)
nodes.statement: Embeds data by reconstructing each point from its $k$ neighbors with linear weights, then finding low-dimensional coordinates that preserve those reconstruction weights subject to a covariance constraint.

nodes.name: Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (SNE)
nodes.statement: Original asymmetric SNE: minimize $\sum_i \mathrm{KL}(P_i \| Q_i)$ with conditional Gaussian probabilities in both spaces, using gradient descent with momentum and simulated annealing via Gaussian noise on $Y$.

nodes.name: UNI-SNE
nodes.statement: Variant of symmetric SNE that adds a uniform background mixing proportion $\rho$ to $q_{ij}$ to introduce slight repulsion between distant points; trained by first running SNE then increasing $\rho$.

nodes.name: Derivation of t-SNE gradient
nodes.statement: Derivation of $\frac{\delta C}{\delta y_i} = 4 \sum_j (p_{ij} - q_{ij})(y_i - y_j)(1 + \|y_i - y_j\|^2)^{-1}$ by chain-rule differentiation of $C = \mathrm{KL}(P \| Q)$ through auxiliary variables $d_{ij} = \|y_i - y_j\|$ and normalizer $Z = \sum_{k \neq l}(1 + d_{kl}^2)^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Introduce auxiliary variables
nodes.statement: Define $d_{ij} = \|y_i - y_j\|$ and $Z = \sum_{k \neq l}(1 + d_{kl}^2)^{-1}$, and observe that varying $y_i$ only changes $d_{ij}$ and $d_{ji}$ for varying $j$.

nodes.name: Apply chain rule via $d_{ij}$
nodes.statement: $\frac{\delta C}{\delta y_i} = \sum_j \left(\frac{\delta C}{\delta d_{ij}} + \frac{\delta C}{\delta d_{ji}}\right)(y_i - y_j) = 2 \sum_j \frac{\delta C}{\delta d_{ij}} (y_i - y_j)$.

nodes.name: Differentiate $\log q_{kl}$ via $\log q_{kl} Z - \log Z$
nodes.statement: Using $C = \sum_{k \neq l} p_{kl} \log p_{kl} - p_{kl} \log q_{kl}$ (constant first part), expand $\log q_{kl} = \log(q_{kl} Z) - \log Z$, and differentiate; only the $k=i, l=j$ term contributes to $\delta(1+d_{kl}^2)^{-1} / \delta d_{ij}$.

nodes.name: Simplify using $\sum_{k \neq l} p_{kl} = 1$
nodes.statement: Obtain $\frac{\delta C}{\delta d_{ij}} = 2(p_{ij} - q_{ij})(1 + d_{ij}^2)^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Conclude gradient
nodes.statement: Substitute into the chain-rule expression to get $\frac{\delta C}{\delta y_i} = 4 \sum_j (p_{ij} - q_{ij})(1 + \|y_i - y_j\|^2)^{-1}(y_i - y_j)$.

nodes.name: Analytical solution to landmark random-walk probabilities
nodes.statement: Sketch (after Grady 2006): the first-hit probability from a non-landmark to a specific landmark equals the solution of the combinatorial Dirichlet problem on the graph Laplacian; reordering landmarks first decomposes the integral, and stationarity gives the linear system $L_N x_N = -B^T$.

nodes.name: Set up Dirichlet integral on Laplacian
nodes.statement: Write $D[x] = \frac{1}{2} x^T L x$ where $L = D - W$ is the graph Laplacian and $D = \mathrm{diag}(\sum_j w_{1j}, \ldots, \sum_j w_{nj})$.

nodes.name: Decompose by reordering landmarks first
nodes.statement: $D[x_N] = \frac{1}{2}(x_L^T L_L x_L + 2 x_N^T B^T x_L + x_N^T L_N x_N)$, where subscripts $L$, $N$ denote landmark and non-landmark blocks.

nodes.name: Differentiate and obtain linear system
nodes.statement: Setting $\delta D[x_N] / \delta x_N = 0$ yields $L_N x_N = -B^T$, nonsingular when each connected component contains a landmark (Biggs 1974).

nodes.name: Cholesky factorization for solving
nodes.statement: Compute $L_N = C C^T$ (Cholesky), then solve $C y = -B^T$ and $C x_N = y$ via fast back-substitution; duplicate landmarks to obtain landmark-to-landmark walk probabilities.

nodes.name: Spring interpretation of SNE gradient
nodes.statement: The SNE gradient acts as the resultant force from springs between $y_i$ and each $y_j$; force direction is $(y_i - y_j)$ and stiffness is the mismatch $(p_{j|i} - q_{j|i} + p_{i|j} - q_{i|j})$.

nodes.name: Asymmetric KL favors local structure
nodes.statement: Because KL is asymmetric, large $p_{j|i}$ modeled by small $q_{j|i}$ incurs heavy cost, so SNE prioritizes preserving local structure.

nodes.name: Student-t inverse-square tail behavior
nodes.statement: $(1 + \|y_i - y_j\|^2)^{-1}$ approaches an inverse-square law for large pairwise distances, making the joint-probability representation almost scale-invariant for distant points.

nodes.name: Long-range forces eliminate need for simulated annealing
nodes.statement: The heavy tails introduce long-range forces that can pull separated clusters of similar points back together, removing the need for simulated annealing used by SNE and UNI-SNE.

nodes.name: Quadratic complexity of t-SNE
nodes.section: 5 Applying t-SNE to Large Data Sets
nodes.statement: Both computational and memory complexity of t-SNE are $O(n^2)$, making the standard version infeasible beyond ~10,000 points and motivating the random-walk variant.

nodes.name: Three weaknesses of t-SNE
nodes.statement: (1) Behavior unclear for general dimensionality reduction beyond $d=3$; (2) sensitive to the curse of intrinsic dimensionality due to local linearity assumption; (3) cost function is non-convex.

nodes.name: MNIST visualization
nodes.statement: t-SNE applied to 6,000 randomly selected MNIST digits (784 dimensions, reduced via PCA to 30) produces an almost-perfect class separation, while Sammon mapping, Isomap, and LLE do not (Figures 2-3).

nodes.name: Olivetti faces visualization
nodes.statement: On 400 face images of 40 individuals (10,304 pixels), t-SNE reveals natural class structure with most individuals' images clustered together (Figure 4).

nodes.name: COIL-20 visualization
nodes.statement: On 1,440 images of 20 objects under 72 viewpoints (1,024 pixels), t-SNE represents each object's one-dimensional viewpoint manifold as a closed loop (Figure 5).

nodes.name: Random-walk t-SNE on full MNIST
nodes.section: 5 Applying t-SNE to Large Data Sets
nodes.statement: Random-walk t-SNE applied to 6,000 landmark digits using all 60,000 MNIST digits ($k=20$ neighbors) yields perfectly separated classes, captures within-class variation (digit orientation, twos' loopiness), and a 1-NN classifier on the 2D map achieves 5.13% error vs.\ 5.75% on the original 784-dimensional data (Figure 7).

nodes.name: Three-landmark random-walk advantage illustration
nodes.section: 5 Applying t-SNE to Large Data Sets
nodes.statement: For three (almost) equidistant landmarks A, B, C with non-landmark points concentrated between A and B, random-walk affinities give $p(A,B) \gg p(A,C)$, while a standard landmark approach treats them equally (Figure 6).
